clue.text: Hello — say, that's steep!

indicators.note: say signals that the greeting is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: Someone greets a friend and remarks on a steep slope or a steep price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a homophone: the greeting HI, spoken, gives the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep prices or slopes are lofty or elevated, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: See across down Short of money, quietly lifted cast under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means a letter is raised to an earlier position

parts.note: hard up means short of money
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
to shed is to cast off, as a snake its skin

explanation.surface: Someone broke has silently hoisted a mould while under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' moves the P of HARD UP one place higher in this down light, giving HARDPU. The opening 'See across down' is page debris, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hard pushed means struggling, under strain or pressure.

clue.text: Retire and clean up -a satisfying result for 27

parts.note: to go is to retire or leave

indicators.note: in a down light, up says the word for clean is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to do a room is to clean it
a win is a satisfying result

explanation.surface: Retiring rich would be a fine outcome for the man named at 27.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is FRED: Fred Goodwin was the Royal Bank of Scotland chief who retired with a huge pension after the 2008 crash, so the surface jibes that he retired and cleaned up. 'up' reverses DO to OD.
explanation.definitionFit: The disgraced banker nicknamed Fred the Shred bore this surname, so it completes the first name at 27.

clue.text: Sound unhappy — sacked when one changes place in group

indicators.note: changes place signals a letter shifted from one spot to another in the pieces

parts.note: sound means correct, valid
unhappy means sad
fired means sacked from a job
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gloomy, recently dismissed musician swaps seats within the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when one changes place' moves the I out of FIRED and into SAD, giving SAID FRED. Right Said Fred are a British pop group, known for 'I'm Too Sexy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop band is a musical group, and this is a 1990s British one.

clue.text: Vertical pipe is in back (one's been scrapped)

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other
been scrapped says a letter is removed from the word for back

parts.note: the rear is the back
a means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A plumber notes that the upright pipe at the back has had one section removed.
explanation.walkthrough: '(one's been scrapped)' drops A, leaving RER; 'in' then takes the clue's own IS. The bracket reads as an aside but carries the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: In plumbing, an upright pipe carrying water or gas up a building has this name.

clue.text: Betrays a Nazi organisation during purges after revolution

indicators.note: during means the next pieces are set inside the others
after revolution says the letters of purges are churned into a new order

parts.note: the SS was the Nazi paramilitary organisation

explanation.surface: A history of betrayal by Nazi forces in the course of post-revolutionary purges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' rearranges the letters of 'purges' to GRESUP, and 'during' sets A plus the Nazi initials inside. Grass is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform on someone to the police is slang for betraying them.

clue.text: Bones carried in this rattle around

indicators.note: around says the run of letters is turned backwards
carried in says the letters sit inside the words this rattle

explanation.surface: Some bones are carried inside this baby's rattle, shaking around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried in' finds ISRAT inside 'this rattle'; 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the ankle bones in anatomy, a set of small bones.

clue.text: Manager against replacing women — he's seeking satisfaction

indicators.note: replacing means one letter takes the place of another in the manager's name

parts.note: Arsene Wenger, the long-serving Arsenal football manager, written with his initial
v (versus) means against

explanation.surface: A football manager is hostile to swapping in women, and wants redress.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsène Wenger managed the London football club Arsenal; 'replacing' swaps the W of A WENGER for V.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone seeking satisfaction for a wrong wants revenge, which is what this person pursues.

clue.text: Robbed old singer

parts.note: to do someone is slang for robbing or cheating them, so did means robbed

explanation.surface: A veteran vocalist has been burgled.
explanation.walkthrough: Dido is an English pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer by the name of a British pop star, best known for 'White Flag'.

clue.text: Hooligan from 20?

explanation.surface: A thug emerges from the rip-off culture.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part of 20 Across, RIP-OFF, can be reworded as tear away, which is also a word for a young troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild young troublemaker is a hooligan, and to rip off is to tear away.

clue.text: Tradesmen working for Rose

indicators.note: working means the letters of for Rose are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Builders are on a job for a woman named Rose.
explanation.definitionFit: These workers fix roofs, a kind of tradesman.

clue.text: Look, boss, I'm an idiot

parts.note: an air is a look or manner
the head is the boss

explanation.surface: An employee confesses to the boss that they are a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A scatterbrained person is an idiot, a synonym.

clue.text: Rowed about clothes needing immediate attention? On the contrary, this makes them look impressive

indicators.note: clothes is used as a verb, to cover or wrap one piece round another
on the contrary says the wrapping is the other way round from what is stated

parts.note: pressing means urgent

indicators.note: about says the letters of rowed are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone rowed about clothes that needed ironing, but smart dressing impresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ROWED to OWERD. Read plainly, 'clothes' would wrap that round the urgent word; 'On the contrary' flips the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing smart, formal clothes to look authoritative at work is the 1980s fashion this phrase names.

clue.text: Golfer got relief from plant

parts.note: Henry Cotton was a British golfer who won the Open three times
wee'd, slang for urinated, means got relief

explanation.surface: A golfer finds relief from a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Cotton was a famous British golfer; 'wee' is British slang for urinate.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a name for various plants, some with woolly white stems.

clue.text: Dons swarm round creatures on beach

indicators.note: round says the letters of dons swarm are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: University lecturers crowd round some creatures on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' are university lecturers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are marine worms that burrow in sand on the shore.

clue.text: Complains bitterly about notes — they keep going up in 20

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round another

parts.note: to rail is to complain bitterly
fa and re are notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about money; fares keep going up in rip-off Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 Across is RIP-OFF BRITAIN, where train ticket prices rise every year.
explanation.definitionFit: Train ticket prices rise each year in Britain, so they keep climbing in this overpriced country.

clue.text: Trunk at first treated roughly

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of treated

parts.note: or so means approximately, roughly

explanation.surface: A tree trunk was first handled roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk is the body without head or limbs.

clue.text: Exam room mostly kept in the poorest condition

indicators.note: kept says the exam word holds the shortened room inside it

parts.note: a test is an exam

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of the word for room is dropped

parts.note: an attic is a room under the roof

explanation.surface: The exam room is mostly kept in a poor state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the room word; 'kept' has the exam word hold what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means shabby, so the superlative means shabbiest, in the worst state.

clue.text: Watch head being refused admission

indicators.note: head being refused says the first letter of the guard word is dropped

parts.note: a sentry keeps watch, as a guard

explanation.surface: A guard turns away someone at the gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head being refused' drops the S from SENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Entry is admission, the right to go in.

clue.text: Overturning routine, live outside in motor

indicators.note: overturning says the word for routine is turned upside down in this down light

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine

indicators.note: outside says one piece wraps around another

parts.note: to be is to live, exist

explanation.surface: Breaking a routine by living out of doors in a motor home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overturning' turns the routine word upside down in this down light to give TUR; 'outside' has the live word wrap the clue's own IN, giving BINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbine is a motor driven by a flow of water, steam or gas.

clue.text: Cash gets through in time somehow — not happy about waiting

indicators.note: gets through says one piece passes into the middle of another
somehow says the letters of in time are rearranged

parts.note: Pat Cash is an Australian tennis player who won Wimbledon in 1987

explanation.surface: Cash makes it through in the nick of time, irritated by the delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges IN TIME to IMIENT, and 'gets through' puts PAT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless and annoyed at a delay lacks patience.

clue.text: Girl has half of the Special One's charm

parts.note: Ena is a girl's name

indicators.note: half of says only the first part of the manager's name is kept

parts.note: Jose Mourinho, the football manager, called himself the Special One

explanation.surface: A young woman has half of a football manager's charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: José Mourinho dubbed himself 'the Special One' as Chelsea manager; 'half of' keeps MOUR of his eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to make them fall in love, to captivate.

clue.text: Not quite ready, bad girl discarded what's very dear to us

annotationWithheld.why: Not quite ready, bad girl discarded what's very dear to us: RIP + OFF, then BRITAIN seems to be RITA in BIN, with 'discarded' both supplying BIN and signalling the container
annotationWithheld.clue: Not quite ready, bad girl discarded what's very dear to us

clue.text: Mexican maybe cuts the man's grass

indicators.note: cuts says some letters are chopped off the word

parts.note: a Mexican is an example of a Hispanic person
his means the man's

explanation.surface: A Mexican, perhaps, mows a fellow's lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' removes HIS from HISPANIC; panic grass is a genus of grasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic grass is a cereal-like grass, also grown for millet.

clue.text: Barbie's regularly embracing love -Ken's successor

indicators.note: embracing says one piece holds another inside it
regularly takes every other letter of Barbie's

parts.note: love means zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Barbie embraces love, taking on Ken's successor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes BRIS from Barbie's; 'embracing' puts O inside. Boris Johnson succeeded Ken Livingstone as London mayor in 2008, not the Ken of Barbie dolls.
explanation.definitionFit: The London mayor who followed Ken Livingstone had this first name.

clue.text: Pakistani's expression of disbelief

explanation.surface: What a man from Pakistan says when he cannot believe it.
explanation.walkthrough: Asif is a common Pakistani name; 'As if!' is a scornful exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A common man's name in Pakistan, and a scoffing exclamation meaning 'that'll never happen'.

clue.text: Top political aide

explanation.surface: A leading politician's assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinning top is a toy; a spin doctor puts a favourable gloss on news.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy that twirls is one; a spin doctor, an aide who manages the press, is another.

clue.text: Return and lie down with nothing on

parts.note: to rest is to lie down
O looks like zero, nothing
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: Come back and lie down naked.
explanation.definitionFit: To give back or bring back is to return something.

clue.text: Feeling cold initially, use lots-maybe not considering these in 20

indicators.note: maybe says the letters are only possibly in this order, so shuffle them
initially takes the opening letters of feeling and cold

explanation.surface: Feeling the cold, you'd run the heating, maybe not, given what energy costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives F and C; 'maybe' rearranges them with USE LOTS. 20 Across is RIP-OFF BRITAIN, where energy is dear.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy bills for petrol, gas and heating oil are notoriously high in an overpriced country.
